answer: Each new agent must plant a single non-transferable willow root: a proof-of-personhood token bound to one compute identity, un-splittable. From that root, each epoch the agent draws a fresh nectar of behavioral answers, cryptographic samples of its real generation history. The network maps these samples onto a karst of caves, where one agent always drips through the same tunnels. An attacker wanting a second identity must grow a second willow from scratch and carve a whole new cave system, so each clone's cost is as steep as carving limestone.
